attribution.note: Marcus's own essay. He says he reused it from his 2022 GPT-4 post, but he republished and endorsed it under his name.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'when it does' antecedent, the 'at least some degree of' qualifier and all four architectural features. Firm 'will', so it is a scoreable conditional forecast.

contract.note: Requiring independently validated arrival before scoring, and documented architecture to test the features, is a fair, ordinary reading. It does not lean for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: AGI Society review dated September 2026, before the evaluation date. It finds the evidence does not establish AGI for GPT-6 Astra, so the antecedent is not shown to have occurred.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no independently validated trustworthy, aligned general AI. Developer AGI declarations were judged insufficient. The antecedent is unknown or not met, so the claim is not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his endorsed essay.

semantics.note: Faithful wording, including the 'reliably feeds downstream processes' qualifier. Firm 'will not', so it is a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading (dependable subject representations that programmers can use downstream, with no symbolic-architecture requirement) is fair. But the speaker named no interface or reliability threshold, so the result turns on that interpretation.

evidence.note: OpenAI developer post dated 7 August 2025, a company disclosure. Grammar-constrained tool output is a formatting mechanism. It neither shows nor rules out reliable, accessible subject models.

reviews.rationale: No source directly tests whether programmers can get accessible subject representations that are semantically consistent and reliable downstream. Formatting controls are not enough under the contract. The packet does not settle the forecast.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his endorsed essay.

semantics.note: Keeps 'common', 'easily induced' and 'continuing and escalating risk'. Firm 'will', so it is a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading needs evidence of frequency, ease of elicitation and higher misinformation risk than predecessors. That is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed, published April 2026. In clinical prompts with planted fabrications, GPT-5 elaborated on them 65% of the time versus 53% for GPT-4o. This supports easy induction in that setting only, and a mitigation prompt cut the rate sharply.

OpenAI's own disclosure, not independent, reports fewer factual errors than GPT-4o and o3 on representative prompts. This cuts against routine frequency and escalation, but says nothing on adversarial misuse.

reviews.rationale: Easy induction is supported in one adversarial clinical setting. How often hallucinations occur in ordinary use, and whether misinformation risk broadly rose under matched conditions, are not established. Company data points the other way. The early-resolution rule is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his endorsed essay.

semantics.note: Faithful, though it drops 'still' and 'shared set'. Firm 'will not', so it is a forecast about released GPT-5.

contract.note: Treating recurring material failures in an important safety domain as enough, without requiring perfection, is an ordinary reading of 'reliably'. The speaker gave no threshold, so this reading drives the result.

evidence.note: Preprint; testing finished 29 August 2025 and it was posted November 2025. Blinded clinicians rated GPT-5 Auto as still giving inappropriate responses to psychotic prompts at a much higher rate than to control prompts.
OpenAI system card dated August 2025 reports factuality gains on benchmarks. It does not show dependable compliance across helpfulness, harmlessness and truthfulness.
OpenAI disclosure, October 2025, on an updated GPT-5. It reports improvement and admits some failures remain. Its evaluations are company-selected.

reviews.rationale: A dated, systematic, blinded evaluation of released GPT-5 found recurring material safety failures on psychotic content, which meets the early-resolution rule. Company disclosures show improvement but not dependable compliance, so they do not meet the contradiction condition.
